title: Placement lease and egress session are separate allocations
summary: API-specific jobs can legitimately require two allocations: a general placement lease followed by an API egress-session reservation. They mesh through identity, requirements, generations and proofs but remain separate authorities.
invariants: A placement lease answers whether the job may execute on a node.
An egress session answers whether an outbound operation may use a particular route now.
Failure to allocate egress does not necessarily invalidate job placement.
Invalid or expired placement must stop browser/job side effects before attempting a new outbound operation.
Current ownership epoch is necessary but not sufficient; requirement, capability, capacity and policy evidence must remain valid.
Long-lived browser sessions must not treat same-node execution as proof that placement is still valid.

provenance.claim: Lease expiry and verification are bound to fresh capacity, capability generation, policy generation and evidence digests.
Allocator defines normal placement/recovery and the separate API work composition.
